description: How ShelfKit itself is built.
---

# TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers with Rust core

## Repository

moon orchestrates tasks and proto pins every toolchain from .prototools. Do not add a task moon does not know about.

## Core logic

The shelf format, validation, revision hashing, and profile resolution live in Rust under crates/. They compile native for the CLI and to WASM for the Worker, so the browser preview and the CLI cannot disagree.

## Storage

One Durable Object per shelf with its own SQLite database, accessed through drizzle-orm/durable-sqlite. There is no D1 database and no cross-shelf query. Content lives in R2 keyed by sha256.

## APM

APM owns install, resolution, and the lockfile. ShelfKit writes apm.yml and stops. Never parse human-oriented apm output: only audit, deps why, pack, policy status, targets, and lock export emit structured data.

## Targets

Use APM's target slugs verbatim. Emit only the OpenAPM v0.1 canonical producer set by default; anything outside it is an explicit opt-in that check must report.

description: The compiler settings this repository relies on.
---

# TypeScript strictness

- strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitOverride, and verbatimModuleSyntax are on. Do not relax them to make code compile.
- Type-only imports must be marked with `import type`.
- No enums and no parameter properties: erasableSyntaxOnly is enabled.

description: Write a conventional commit message for the staged changes.
argument-hint: "[scope]"
---

Read the staged diff and write one conventional commit message.

Rules:
- Subject line in the imperative mood, no trailing period, at most 72 characters.
- Type is one of feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, test, perf, build, ci.
- Include a body only when the change needs a reason that the subject cannot carry.
- Do not mention that the change was generated, and do not list files.
